lines.trans: Two firm pillows under your heel, Salma, and strict orders not to touch the floor.
Fine, fine—if I cannot stand at the stove, listen carefully to my kitchen rules!
Clipboard ready, Chef Salma! Who gets the six-o'clock bread dough?
Ziad has strong shoulders—he kneads the morning dough while I watch the timer.
Deal! I used to help my grandmother knead Sunday loaves every week.
And who whisks the lemon curd and chops carrots for the lentil soup?
You whisk the lemons at my elbow, Nour, and Rami chops every vegetable to the millimetre!
Believe me, Rami will measure every carrot cube with a ruler!
What job do we give Mazen so he feels helpful without breaking anything?
Polishing the twelve white cups at the table—far away from switches and paint!
Now drink this chamomile tea and go rest upstairs, Salma.
Wake me at six sharp—nobody touches my oven without me in that chair!

See you soon!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite having no -a ending; means ground, land, or indoor floor.

examples.trans: The floor is clean and dry now.
Set the box on the floor for a moment.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: Plural أوامر means 'orders / instructions' (أوزع أوامر 'hand out orders').

examples.text: الشيف سلمى جاهزة توزع أوامر عالفريق كله!
examples.trans: Chef Salma is ready to issue orders to the whole team!

examples.text: تحت أمرك يا معلم، الشيش صار جاهز للتركيب.
examples.trans: At your service, boss—the shutters are ready to mount.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one woman.

examples.trans: You must be Nour!
You are today's heroine, Nour.

meanings.note: Said on its own, اتفقنا ('we agreed') is the everyday way to close a deal: 'deal!'.

examples.text: اتفقنا، بنلتقي الساعة تسعة عند الباب.
examples.trans: Agreed, we meet at nine at the door.

examples.text: اتفقت مع سلمى على كيكة الجمعة.
examples.trans: I agreed with Salma about the Friday cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برتاح, بيرتاح).

examples.trans: Rest up after your journey, ma'am.
We rested in the courtyard with a glass of tea.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb meaning both 'receive a delivery' and 'take over a station/duty'.

examples.text: زياد بيستلم قسم الشوربة وتقشير الخضار.
examples.trans: Ziad takes charge of the soup and vegetable-peeling station.

examples.text: استلمنا الطحين الطازة من الفرن الصبح.
examples.trans: We received the fresh flour from the bakery in the morning.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'twelve'; before a singular counted noun it takes -r: اطنعشر دقة ('twelve chimes').

examples.trans: The clock tower chimed twelve!
Here is twelve dinars change.

meanings.note: First working day of the Jordanian week (pronounced il-ahad).

examples.text: يوم الأحد الصبح بنرتب جدول الأسبوع كله.
examples.trans: On Sunday morning we plan the schedule for the whole week.

examples.text: المدارس والمكاتب بعمان بتفتح يوم الأحد.
examples.trans: Schools and offices in Amman open on Sunday.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Uncountable herbal noun; شاي بابونج ('chamomile tea') is a beloved soothing Levantine infusion.

examples.text: غليت إبريق بابونج دافي عشان ترتاح سلمى.
examples.trans: I brewed a warm pot of chamomile tea so Salma could relax.

examples.text: ريحة البابونج مع العسل بتهدي الأعصاب بالليل.
examples.trans: The scent of chamomile with honey calms the nerves at night.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بعيدة, plural: بعاد).

examples.trans: The shop is not far from the gate.

examples.text: الطاولة تحت الشجرة بعيد عن الباب.
examples.trans: The table is under the tree away from the door.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: Affectionate Levantine family word for 'grandmother' (often used directly without a possessive suffix).

examples.text: وصفة شوربة العدس هاي تعلمتها من تيتا.
examples.trans: I learned this lentil soup recipe from my grandma.

examples.text: تيتا دايما بتحط قشر ليمون طازة مع الكيك.
examples.trans: Grandma always puts fresh lemon zest into her cakes.

meanings.note: Feminine plural جامدات also appears in Jordanian speech for firm fruit (متل ليمونات جامدات).

examples.text: نقي ليمونات صفر وجامدات عشان تارت الليمون.
examples.trans: Pick firm yellow lemons for the lemon tarts.

examples.text: الكريمة بردت بالبراد وصارت جامدة ومتماسكة.
examples.trans: The curd chilled in the fridge and turned firm and set.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Collective noun جزر ('carrots') with singulative جزرة ('one carrot').

examples.text: فرمنا الجزر والبصل لمكعبات صغيرة ومتساوية.
examples.trans: We diced the carrots and onions into small, even cubes.

examples.text: الجزر المشوي بيعطي الشوربة حلاوة طبيعية.
examples.trans: Roasted carrots give the soup a natural sweetness.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: With possessive endings, حال acts as 'myself/yourself/itself' (لحاله by itself, لا تغلبي حالك don't tire yourself).

examples.trans: The door opened by itself from the wind.
How are you doing today?

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحس, بيحس).

examples.text: نتمنى كل ضيف يحس بالراحة هون.
examples.trans: We hope every guest feels at home here.
I felt the warmth the moment I walked in.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Salma cooked hot vegetable soup.
We bought fresh vegetables from the market.

meanings.note: Culinary verb for whisking eggs, lemon curd, or cream until smooth.

examples.text: نور بتخفق البيض مع الليمون والسكر بهدوء.
examples.trans: Nour whisks the eggs gently with lemon and sugar.

examples.text: خفقت سلمى الكريمة حتى صارت ناعمة ومتساوية.
examples.trans: Salma whisked the curd until it turned smooth and glossy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Form III verb meaning 'keep a close eye on an oven, timer, or process'.

examples.text: أبو طارق بيراقب درجة حرارة الفرن والمؤقت.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq watches the oven temperature and the timer.

examples.text: أنا براقب من الكرسي وبعطيكم التعليمات.
examples.trans: I'll watch from the chair and give you instructions.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشرب, بيشرب).

examples.trans: Drink hot tea first.

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من شوربة الخضار.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the vegetable soup.

meanings.note: Versatile spoken Levantine noun meaning 'task / job / matter'.

examples.text: ضل علينا تلات شغلات بسيطة قبل يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: We only have three simple tasks left before Wednesday.

examples.text: تذوق الكيك هو أحلى شغلة بالكافيه كله!
examples.trans: Tasting cake is the best job in the entire café!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شوربات.

examples.trans: Here is a cup of hot vegetable soup.
Hot soup is wonderful on a rainy day.

meanings.note: Used across modern Jordanian kitchens and cafés for both male and female head chefs.

examples.text: الدفتر جاهز يا شيف سلمى، بشو نبلش؟
examples.trans: The clipboard is ready, Chef Salma—what do we start with?

examples.text: الشيف ذاق الشوربة وابتسم من أول معلقة.
examples.trans: The chef tasted the soup and smiled from the very first spoonful.

meanings.note: Describes strict rules or a no-nonsense chef's standards.

examples.text: تعليمات سلمى بالمطبخ صارمة وواضحة للكل.
examples.trans: Salma's instructions in the kitchen are strict and clear to everyone.

examples.text: مازن التزم بموعد النشفان بنظام صارم.
examples.trans: Mazen stuck to the drying schedule with strict discipline.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصحى, بيصحى).

examples.trans: Room four wakes up at quarter past seven.
I woke up early to the birdsong.

meanings.note: Form II verb disambiguated with shadda from noun صدق ('truth'); صدقوني = 'believe me!'.

examples.text: صدقوني، رح تشغلوا بالكم أكتر من العادة!
examples.trans: Believe me, you're going to work even harder than usual!

examples.text: ما صدقت قديش صوت البيانو صار صافي ودافي.
examples.trans: I couldn't believe how clear and warm the piano sounded.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Describes kind-hearted people (ناس طيبين) and pleasant smells/tastes (ريحة طيبة); standalone طيب means 'alright / well then'.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
The coffee smells wonderful in the morning!

meanings.note: Core bakery verb for kneading bread or pastry dough.

examples.text: طارق بيعجن عجينة التارت بإيدين ثابتة.
examples.trans: Tariq kneads the tart dough with steady hands.

examples.text: سلمى عجنت العجين بكير عشان يرتاح قبل الفجر.
examples.trans: Salma kneaded the dough early so it could rest before dawn.

meanings.note: Used for baking dough.

examples.trans: The bread dough is ready in the oven.
She left the dough to rest half an hour.

meanings.note: Collective noun; شوربة عدس ('golden lentil soup' with lemon and olive oil) is a beloved Jordanian staple.

examples.text: شوربة العدس مع عصرة ليمون أطيب غدا بالشتا.
examples.trans: Lentil soup with a squeeze of lemon is the best lunch on a rainy day.

examples.text: سلمى غسلت العدس الأصفر وحطته عالنار.
examples.trans: Salma rinsed the yellow lentils and set them on the stove.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) vocalized to distinguish it from verb عجن ('to knead').

examples.text: طارق بلش بعجن الطحين والزبدة الباردة للتارت.
examples.trans: Tariq started kneading the flour and cold butter for the tarts.

examples.text: العجن الهادئ بيخلي قشرة التارت هشة ومقرمشة.
examples.trans: Gentle kneading keeps the tart crust tender and flaky.

meanings.note: In Jordanian homes and kitchens, الغاز routinely means 'the kitchen stove / range'.

examples.text: حطيت طنجرة الشوربة عالغاز على نار هادية.
examples.trans: I set the soup pot on the stove over a gentle flame.

examples.text: طفي الغاز لما يصفر المؤقت بعد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: Turn off the stove when the timer rings in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine kitchen verb for chopping vegetables or herbs.

examples.text: زياد بيقشر البصل وبيفرم الجزر للشوربة.
examples.trans: Ziad peels the onions and chops the carrots for the soup.

examples.text: فرمت ضمة بقدونس طازة فوق الصحن.
examples.trans: I chopped a fresh bunch of parsley over the dish.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فناجين.

examples.trans: I set two teacups on the tray.
This is my favourite coffee cup.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقيس, بيقيس).

examples.trans: I measure quietness and acoustics in courtyards.
The shopkeeper measured it against the old valve.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قواعد.

examples.text: أول قاعدة: اشرب شاي سخن الصبح!
examples.trans: Rule one: drink hot tea in the morning!
The work rules here are simple and clear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'in front of, before'.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns against the evening sky.
The car is parked in front of the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural is قوايا (qawaaya): كرسيين قوايا ('two sturdy chairs').

examples.trans: The gate rang with one strong ring.
We brought two sturdy wooden chairs to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كتاف.

examples.trans: Square your shoulders and smile with confidence!
He carried the heavy bag on his shoulder.

meanings.note: An everyday item of furniture for sitting.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Culinary noun used for كريمة الليمون ('lemon curd / cream') and pastry fillings.

examples.text: نور جهزت كريمة الليمون الصفرا للتارت.
examples.trans: Nour prepared the bright yellow lemon curd for the tarts.

examples.text: ريحة كريمة الليمون الطازة عبت المطبخ كله.
examples.trans: The aroma of fresh lemon curd filled the entire kitchen.

meanings.note: Transitive Form I verb ('break something, break up visual monotony').

examples.text: الخشب الجاف بيكسر حدة الحجر بالساحة.
examples.trans: Warm dry wood breaks up the starkness of the courtyard stone.

examples.text: انتبه لا تكسر المرطبان القزاز عالرف.
examples.trans: Be careful not to break the glass jar on the shelf.

meanings.note: Names the heel of a foot or shoe (كعب القدم / كعب الحذاء).

examples.text: زحلق كعب حذائي عن حرف الطبلية الواطية.
examples.trans: The heel of my shoe slipped off the edge of the low stool.

examples.text: اسندي كعبك عالوسادة الطرية عشان ترتاح رجلك.
examples.trans: Rest your heel on the soft cushion so your foot can relax.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمس, بيلمس).

examples.trans: Touch the radiator — it is warm on top.
Touch the brass pipe — it heated up!

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Kitchen or oven timer (from وقت 'time').

examples.text: عيرت المؤقت على تمنطاعشر دقيقة للتارت.
examples.trans: I set the timer for eighteen minutes for the tarts.

examples.text: أبو طارق عينه عالمؤقت عشان ما يتحمر الخبز زيادة.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq keeps his eye on the timer so the bread doesn't over-brown.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مخدات.

examples.trans: I put two soft pillows on the bed.
The cotton pillow is comfortable for sleeping.

meanings.note: Used for measuring and drawing crisp straight lines on signs or labels.

examples.text: سطرت نور الملصقين بالمسطرة وقلم الحبر الأسود.
examples.trans: Nour ruled both labels with a straightedge and a black ink pen.

examples.text: قيس الحروف بالمسطرة عشان تطلع بوسط اللوحة.
examples.trans: Measure the letters with the ruler so they sit centered on the sign.

meanings.note: Vocalized with shadda to distinguish passive participle مشبّك ('clipped', لوح مشبّك = clipboard) from noun مشبك ('clasp/clip').

examples.text: نور مسكت اللوح المشبك وسجلت مهام يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: Nour held the clipboard and wrote down Wednesday's tasks.

examples.text: الورق مشبك ببعضه عشان ما يطير مع الهوا.
examples.trans: The sheets are clipped together so they don't blow away in the breeze.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Used for ice cubes (مكعب تلج), sugar cubes, and diced vegetables.

examples.text: دوق الشوربة وشوف إذا بدها كمان مكعب جزر.
examples.trans: Taste the soup and see if it needs another cube of carrot.

examples.text: لفينا مكعبات التلج بمنشفة قطن نضيفة.
examples.trans: We wrapped the ice cubes in a clean cotton towel.

meanings.note: Standard measurement unit, borrowed into Arabic.

examples.trans: The ring width is twenty millimetres exactly.
He measured the part to the millimetre.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian distal demonstrative ('that over there / that past...'); feminine هديك (hadiik), plural هدولاك.

examples.text: بتذكر هداك الربيع لما فتحنا النزل؟
examples.trans: Do you remember that spring when we opened the inn?

examples.text: حط الصندوق على هداك الرف العالي.
examples.trans: Put the box on that high shelf.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Third person masculine pronoun.

examples.trans: He knows heritage law well.

examples.text: بيحكي هيك وهو بيطل من الشباك!
examples.trans: He says that while peeking out the window!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
